_strings.@@59ae97179379: Treaty conformity — UT conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from UT income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the UT return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Utah's resident return (TC-40) starts from federal adjusted gross income (FAGI). 2024 TC-40 Line 4 is "Federal adjusted gross income from federal return." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from FAGI and flows through. The full list of 2024 TC-40A Part 1 "Additions to Income (added to federal income)" — codes 51 (lump sum distribution), 53 (MSA addback), 54 (my529 addback), 56 (child's income excluded from parent's return), 57 (municipal bond interest), 60 (untaxed income of a resident trust), 61 (untaxed income of a nonresident trust), 67 (tax paid on behalf of a pass-through entity taxpayer), 68 (PPP grant/loan addback), 69 (equitable adjustments) — contains NO add-back of income exempt under a federal tax treaty (the code list is unchanged from 2023). The instructions' "Income from Other Countries" section reinforces this: Utah residents pay Utah tax on income earned in other countries only "if the income is included in federal adjusted gross income on the federal return." Therefore treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by Utah -> conforms = true.

_strings.@@5bfa03d04271: Taxpayer Tax Credit — Available to essentially all Utah resident filers (and apportioned for part-year/nonresidents). It is the broad general credit that offsets Utah's flat 4.55% income tax. The credit is reduced (phased out) as income rises above a base amount tied to filing status, and is reduced to zero for higher earners. Filers whose federal AGI is at or below their federal standard deduction are instead 'Qualified Exempt Taxpayers' and owe no Utah tax (TC-40 line 21).

_strings.@@6ccd4ea3dece: At-Home Parent Credit — An at-home parent (biological/step/adoptive/foster parent, legal guardian, or person housing a child placed by a child-placing agency for legal adoption) who provides full-time care in their residence for a child 12 months old or younger on the last day of 2024, with the child claimed as a dependent on the at-home parent's return. The at-home parent's combined W-2 wages/tips/compensation plus federal Schedule C gross income (line 7) must be $3,000 or less, and federal adjusted gross income (TC-40 line 4) must be $50,000 or less. Nonrefundable; no carryforward/back.
_strings.@@ab07094ca27d: Retirement Credit — You (and/or your spouse, if filing jointly) must have been born on or before Dec. 31, 1952. You may NOT claim it if you (or your spouse) claim either the Social Security Benefits Credit (code AH) or the Military Retirement Credit (code AJ). Nonrefundable: reduces tax to zero but no refund of excess; no carryforward/back.
_strings.@@ad6801b53115: 2024 Utah TC-40 Individual Income Tax Instructions, Child Tax Credit (UC 59-10-1047) and Child Tax Credit Worksheet, p.22; What's New (HB 170)
_strings.@@be64201f185d: UT state income tax (2024, flat rate): taxable_base $40,000.00 — which must be the state's own income base derived from federal AGI plus/minus the state's additions and subtractions (NOT raw federal AGI when modifications apply) — with no exemptions or standard deduction to subtract; tax = 0.0455 x $40,000 = $1,82
_strings.@@d7af57c79734: Social Security Benefits Credit — Available to filers who included taxable Social Security benefits in income. This is Utah's senior/retirement-income relief credit (an alternative to, and larger than, the Retirement Credit for many). You may NOT also claim the Retirement Credit (code 18) for the same person. Nonrefundable: reduces tax to zero, no refund of excess, no carryforward/back.
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.
_strings.@@ed07b015fd3d: Utah Child Tax Credit (NEW for 2024) — Created by HB 170 (2023 Utah Legislature), first claimable for tax year 2024. Available for each child who (1) qualifies for the federal child tax credit under IRC 24, and (2) was at least one year old and no more than three years old on the last day of 2024. Phased out by modified adjusted gross income. Nonrefundable; no carryforward/back.
_strings.@@ee54f24546b9: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW credit, first claimable for tax year 2024: the Utah Child Tax Credit, created by HB 170 (2023 Utah Legislature) and codified at UC 59-10-1047. It is $1,000 per child who qualifies for the federal child tax credit under IRC 24 and was at least one year old and no more than three years old on the last day of 2024, reduced by 10% of modified adjusted gross income above the filing-status threshold ($27,000 MFS / 1040NR; $54,000 MFJ; $43,000 single, QSS or head of household), not below zero. Nonrefundable, with no carryforward or carryback; claimed on TC-40A Part 3 with code AT. Resolve via: 2024 Utah TC-40 Individual Income Tax Instructions, Child Tax Credit (UC 59-10-1047) and Child Tax Credit Worksheet, p.22 (the citation URL) for the age test and the MAGI phase-out; calc.state_tax returns TC-40 line 10 and applies no TC-40A credits.
_strings.@@f275825beaa9: Utah Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — You must (1) qualify for and claim the federal earned income tax credit in the same tax year, and (2) earn Utah income reported on a federal W-2. The credit is limited to the amount of Utah wages (Earned Income Tax Credit Worksheet: enter the lesser of 20% of the federal credit or total Utah W-2 box 16 wages). Nonrefundable: it can reduce Utah income tax to zero but any excess is not refunded and cannot be carried forward or back.

Tax line: Form TC-40 Line 10: 'Utah tax - multiply line 9 by 4.55% (.0455) (not less than zero)' (Line 9 = Utah taxable income/loss = Line 6 total income minus Lines 7-8; Line 4 starts from federal AGI). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Rate change for 2024: SB 69 (2024 General Session) lowered Utah's flat individual income tax rate from 4.65% to 4.55% (2024 TC-40 instructions, What's New; the 4.55% rate is printed on Line 10 of the 2024 TC-40 itself). Base guidance: supply 2024 Form TC-40 Line 9 'Utah taxable income/loss' — Line 4 federal adjusted gross income plus Line 5 additions (TC-40A Part 1, codes 51-69) minus Line 7 (state tax refund included on federal Schedule 1, line 1) and Line 8 subtractions (TC-40A Part 2, codes 71-90). The op multiplies it by 4.55%, producing the Line 10 tax before credits. CRITICAL — Taxpayer Tax Credit (TC-40 Lines 11-20, NOT modeled): Utah has no standard deduction and no base personal exemptions; their function is replaced by a nonrefundable CREDIT against the Line 10 tax. Line 16 initial credit = 6% (.06) of [Line 11 Utah personal exemption ($2,046 x line 2d qualifying dependents — dependents ONLY, not taxpayer/spouse) + Line 12 federal standard or itemized deductions - Line 14 state income tax from federal form 1040, Schedule A, line 5a]. It phases out at 1.3% (.013) of Line 9 income above the Line 17 base: $17,652 single or married filing separately; $26,478 head of household; $35,304 married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse. Line 22 Utah income tax = Line 10 minus Line 20 (not less than zero). This op returns the LINE 10 amount — compute Lines 11-22 on the form. exemptions ships empty and standard_deduction ships null intentionally: the $2,046 personal exemption and the federal standard/itemized deduction are inputs to the Line 20 CREDIT, never subtractions from the Line 9 base — pass exemptions_count=0 and dependents_count=0. Qualified exempt taxpayer (TC-40 Line 21, NOT modeled): if federal adjusted gross income is less than or equal to the federal standard deduction (excluding the extra age-65/blind amounts), the filer is exempt from Utah income tax entirely — check the Line 21 worksheet before relying on the computed tax. Zero floor: Line 10 prints 'not less than zero' — a Line 9 loss produces $0 tax (the op clamps a negative base to $0). Rounding (instructions p.3, 'Rounding Off to Whole Dollars'): 'Round off cents to the nearest whole dollar. Round down if under 50 cents; round up if 50 cents and above' — matches this op's whole-dollar rounding. Not modeled — credits and later lines: apportionable nonrefundable credits on Line 24 (TC-40A Part 3, e.g. the 20%-of-federal Utah EITC code AM, the $450 retirement credit code 18, the Social Security benefits credit code AH at 4.55%, and the NEW 2024 $1,000-per-child ages-1-3 child tax credit code AT from HB 170), nonapportionable credits (Line 26), use tax (Line 31), and the TC-40B non/part-year resident apportionment (Line 25) all come after Line 10 on the form.
